_comment: Candidate sources for the public demo's seed bundle (issue #628). Each seeded file lands in the named `collection` (ids in app.scripts.demo_seed.bundle.COLLECTIONS). Every item built from these must pass `python -m app.scripts.demo_seed validate`, and each source's licence page must be re-read and dated in license_checked_on at bundle build (docs-site/docs/operations/public-demo.md). Only the speech of people speaking in an official or professional public capacity is used; no private individual. `exclusions` are rules the curator applies when choosing recordings; FCC and OSHA were dropped on 2026-11-08 because their licence pages could not be read (see `excluded`); every remaining source's licence page was re-read that day except LibriVox, which stays out pending the owner's decision. The owner approves the final item list. Neutrality review 2026-11-08: the owner rejected the first picks as not politically neutral; the list now covers science, space, weather, technology, culture, education, how-to and statistics explainers only. The government-meetings collection is filled with NASA meetings and USGS public lectures, so a rename to 'Government meetings & public talks' is proposed for the owner (COLLECTIONS unchanged).

sources.name: Voice of America features in several languages (science, technology, culture, lifestyle, economy explainers)
sources.why_allowed: VOA's copyright page: "All text, audio and video material produced exclusively by the Voice of America is in the public domain." Page checked 2026-11-08.
exclusions: Exclude any segment not produced exclusively by VOA: the page says some material is licensed for VOA programming only and is not public domain, and AFP, AP and Reuters material may not be redistributed.
Exclude street interviews and vox pops with private individuals; keep only VOA staff, officials and named experts speaking in a professional capacity.

Neutral topics only: no elections, politics, conflict, crime, immigration or individuals' cases; sports and entertainment items were not taken because they usually carry third-party game, film or music footage that VOA's public-domain statement does not cover.

sources.name: NASA Advisory Council and NASA town hall meetings
sources.why_allowed: NASA media guidelines (re-read 2026-11-08): NASA content 'generally [is] not subject to copyright in the United States'.
exclusions: Opening ~13 minutes only; Q&A cut.
The Exploration Systems town hall touches the proposed federal budget in its opening; owner to confirm it is neutral enough.

sources.name: USGS public lecture series (PubTalks)
sources.why_allowed: USGS Copyrights and Credits (re-read 2026-11-08): 'USGS-authored or produced data and information are considered to be in the U.S. Public Domain'; non-USGS images used with permission are marked, and USGS staff voice or likeness may carry publicity rights for commercial use.
exclusions: Opening ~13 minutes only; audience Q&A with members of the public cut.
Verify from transcripts that no guest speaker or copyrighted slide-only content is relied on.

sources.name: Bureau of Labor Statistics explainer videos
sources.why_allowed: BLS Copyright Information: 'everything that we publish, both in hard copy and electronically, is in the public domain, except for previously copyrighted photographs and illustrations.' Read 2026-11-08 from the Internet Archive copy (bls.gov returns 403 to scripts).
exclusions: Short narrated explainers; no members of the public.

sources.name: Federal Reserve FOMC introductory statements (Chair's prepared remarks)
sources.attribution: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.why_allowed: Board website: its information "is in the public domain and may be copied and distributed without permission"; credit the Board. Checked 2026-11-08.
exclusions: Chair's prepared introductory statement only; only statements without tariff, immigration or other policy-contested passages.

sources.name: SEC open meetings
sources.why_allowed: The SEC's website dissemination policy is the 'Website Dissemination' section of the page titled Privacy Information (there is no separate copyright page): information may be copied or further distributed without the SEC's permission, cite the SEC as the source, and do not use the SEC seal or other logos and artwork. Re-read 2026-11-08. Commission-produced recordings only.
exclusions: Opening minutes only; only technical rule topics (foreign private issuer definition, market-structure rule); no climate-disclosure, enforcement or crypto meetings.

sources.name: Bureau of Labor Statistics career-information videos
sources.why_allowed: Same BLS Copyright Information page: public domain except previously copyrighted photographs and illustrations.
exclusions: How-to-use-the-tool videos only.

sources.name: NOAA National Ocean Service education video
sources.why_allowed: NOS disclaimers (re-read 2026-11-08): 'Information presented on this website is considered public information and may be distributed or copied, unless specifically noted otherwise.' Wording is 'public information', not 'public domain'.
exclusions: NOAA seal and initials not used as branding.

sources.name: NASA education videos and podcasts
sources.why_allowed: NASA media guidelines: NASA content "generally [is] not subject to copyright in the United States" and factual, non-endorsing use needs no permission. Checked 2026-11-08. This is not a blanket public-domain grant, hence the exclusions.
exclusions: Exclude items labelled with a third-party copyright holder's name (NASA's permission does not extend to others).
Exclude children, students or other private individuals on camera or on the audio; keep NASA staff and astronauts in their official role.
Never use NASA's insignia, or a NASA employee's name or likeness, to imply endorsement.

sources.name: FEMA preparedness how-to videos
sources.why_allowed: FEMA website information page, re-read 2026-11-08: 'Most material on FEMA.gov is free of copyright and may be copied and distributed without permission'; licensed or restricted photos and graphics carry a credit or copyright notice and need the source's permission; use of the DHS seal and marks is restricted.
exclusions: Preparedness how-to and risk explainers only; no survivors, disaster footage, recovery or disaster-response operations.

sources.name: National Weather Service forecast-office briefings (outlook and water supply)
sources.why_allowed: NWS disclaimer (re-read 2026-11-08): NWS web information 'is in the public domain, unless specifically noted otherwise'.
exclusions: Outlooks and water-supply briefings only.

sources.name: NASA Goddard explainer videos
sources.why_allowed: NASA media guidelines (re-read 2026-11-08): generally not subject to copyright in the US; third-party material is marked.
exclusions: Narrated explainers, no one on camera; background-music provenance to confirm.

sources.name: NASA mission briefings and NASA TV programmes
sources.why_allowed: NASA media guidelines: content "generally [is] not subject to copyright in the United States". Checked 2026-11-08.
exclusions: Opening part of each briefing only; reporter Q&A cut. No climate-policy, budget-politics or defence-programme briefings.

sources.name: NOAA and National Weather Service briefings
sources.why_allowed: NWS disclaimer: its information "is in the public domain, unless specifically noted otherwise"; do not imply endorsement or alter it as official. Checked 2026-11-08.
exclusions: Forecaster briefings only; hurricane briefings limited to track and intensity forecasts, no damage reports.

sources.name: Redaction showcase: a scripted clip voiced by the project team with invented names, numbers and addresses
sources.why_allowed: Written and voiced by the project team and dedicated to CC0. Every personal detail is invented and the item is marked synthetic_pii: true.
exclusions: No real person's details; invented names, numbers and addresses only.

excluded.name: FDA advisory committee meetings
excluded.reason: Dropped 2026-11-08 (owner neutrality rule): drugs, vaccines and medical controversy.

excluded.name: NTSB board meetings
excluded.reason: Dropped 2026-11-08 (owner neutrality rule): accident and fatality investigations.

excluded.name: VOA reports on elections, conflict, security, immigration, politics and individual legal cases
excluded.reason: Dropped 2026-11-08 (owner neutrality rule); 11 of 13 previous VOA items.

excluded.name: FEMA disaster-response, registration and tribal-recovery videos; NASA climate, budget-politics and defence briefings; Fed statements and SEC meetings touching tariffs, immigration, climate rules, enforcement or crypto; a hurricane briefing quoting fatality figures
excluded.reason: Dropped 2026-11-08 (owner neutrality rule); see the archive README's removed list.

excluded.name: NSF National Science Board, NOAA Library talks, Library of Congress talks, ESA videos
excluded.reason: Not taken: no licence page could be read for NSF (404) or NOAA Library content, Library of Congress rights are item-by-item, and no ESA item was verified as CC BY or CC BY-SA IGO.

excluded.name: AMI Meeting Corpus
excluded.reason: CC BY 4.0, but the speakers are private individuals; the demo carries no private individual's voice.

excluded.name: Company earnings calls
excluded.reason: Company-owned content, not a government work or openly licensed.

excluded.name: Any Creative Commons NC or ND licence
excluded.reason: Not in the allowed licence list; NC forbids the demo's promotional use and ND forbids the transcript and summary derivatives.

excluded.name: Public-comment and open-hearing segments (FCC, FDA, SEC, NTSB)
excluded.reason: Private citizens speak; cut them from every meeting.

excluded.name: FCC open commission meetings
excluded.reason: Dropped 2026-11-08: the agency's own copyright/use page could not be read (FCC returned 403, OSHA's disclaimer and privacy URLs returned 404). 17 U.S.C. 105 would normally cover agency works, but the demo's rule is to cite and re-read the agency's own terms, so the source stays out until a person reads the page. Reinstate by reading the page and adding a source entry.

excluded.name: OSHA training and safety videos
excluded.reason: Dropped 2026-11-08: the agency's own copyright/use page could not be read (FCC returned 403, OSHA's disclaimer and privacy URLs returned 404). 17 U.S.C. 105 would normally cover agency works, but the demo's rule is to cite and re-read the agency's own terms, so the source stays out until a person reads the page. Reinstate by reading the page and adding a source entry.
